title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
read_level: partial (arXiv HTML v1: abstract, Secs 1-3, Tables 1-4, Sec 6 discussion/conclusion, impact statement, reference list; Secs 4-5 body and Appendices A-G skimmed)
why_wsp: An automated analytical 5-stage compiler (no LLM author) grafts closed-form arithmetic and Boolean circuits into pretrained LM weights via width extension; it cites WSP only as a concurrent paradigm in a conceptual comparison table and does not position itself as a WSP baseline or replacement.
exclusion_reason: Closed-form compiler with no LLM editor; WSP is cited only as a concurrent, conceptually compared paradigm (Table 1, Sec 2), not as something it baselines or replaces.
facets: application domain: exact arithmetic in pretrained LMs
domain: compiling exact multi-digit arithmetic and Boolean circuits into pretrained LMs
editor: none (analytical compiler: "An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed {+,-,x} circuits")
target: IBM Granite 4.2 3B, Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B; Gemma 4 E4B (Boolean audits only)
interface: closed form (analytical primitives; width extension d -> d+K)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M - 1.33M active non-zeros, <= 0.036%) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M - 2.39M non-zeros, <= 0.057%)" (Abstract); added width K=1,140 (Granite) / 2,555 (Qwen) (Table 2).

headline_results.quote: reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98% - 100% mid-sentence resumption
3-literal Boolean (100%, N=1,728; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits
both grafts pass all 14/14 expanded reasoning and >2K-token splits (N=4,392

cost.quote: holds A100 memory at 7.89 / 10.65 GiB (4.60 / 8.14 GiB under INT8 / INT4 + FP32 sidecar)

baselines_and_controls: Pretrained base; external Python router (PAL-style); same-backbone LoRA SFT on 12.8K examples; fixed-d coordinate and SVD projection controls; five-primitive leave-one-out ablations.
runs_and_variance: Four seeds x 8 formats (N=3,000 per model): "Four-seed 8-format evaluation (N=3,000/model) reaches 94.07% / 96.60%" (Sec 5); Wilson CIs in Table 12.
robustness_of_edits: Pure BF16 shows carry drift (4/5 G3-G7 in BF16, 5/5 in FP32); circuits kept in FP32 sidecar survive INT8/INT4 quantization of W_NL: "maintains 100.0% Qwen arithmetic across BF16 / INT8 / INT4" (Sec 5).
verification: Formal IEEE 754 / TF32 error bounds (Theorem 3.2); BF16 1-ULP correctness stated as empirical only.
limitations_stated: Division omitted from main layout; unbounded-length inputs exceed single-pass TC0; full Gemma 4 arithmetic and fused kernels open; dense padding inflates parameters 1.98-3.13x; dual-use risk of dormant triggered payloads.
code_or_data: none found (paper names sparse_sidecar_runtime.py and standalone patches but gives no URL)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (cited as concurrent)
Hu et al. 2026, Exploring weight-space programming, arXiv 2611.09382 (cited as concurrent)
RASP, Tracr, Tracr-Injection, Percepta CALM VM
notes_for_survey: Excluded: no LLM determines the weights. Its Table 1 lists 'Agentic WSP' as a conceptual comparison and Sec 2 says WSP "heuristically perturbs ~10^3 scalars". Possible related-work pointer for hand-compiled circuits in pretrained LMs and for the dormant-trigger security note.
